newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece aims to tame inflation via social dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Greece aims to tame inflation via social dialogue.

text.p: The government will try to forge a national consensus on reducing inflation through social dialogue to be announced today by the government, said National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou.

"The reduction in inflation is not only the responsibility of the government," Papandoniou told financial daily Kerdos. "Businessmen, workers, owners of real estate, all must tone down their nominal claims for increased income so that, with the fall in inflation, we can better ensure their real income."
The business world held a key role in meeting the government's call for self-restraint, said Papandoniou.
The government would do its part to trim deficits, freeze indirect taxes and keep a lid on increases in public utility tariffs as well as follow a strict monetary and exchange policy.

The government's social dialogue, to be announced today by Prime Minister Costas Simitis, is an effort to find common ground on economic and social policies with all social groups, through talks over the coming weeks.

CPI inflation was 6.8 percent year-on-year in January, the lowest figure in 25 years, and there was optimism at the national economy and finance ministry of a 6.5 percent figure in February, 6.0 percent in March, with inflation breaking through the 6.0 percent barrier in April.
The government hopes to achieve 4.5 percent year-on-year inflation by the end of the year, which critics have called ambitious. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
